title: Legal sacrifices foreshadowing Christ were not clear faith for OT believers — revelation measures faith
source_text: XXVII. Praeterea contendunt, sub toto Veteris Testamenti curriculo in Ecclesia scitu necessarium fuisse, quod sacrificia legalia futurum Christi sacrificium adumbrarent. Id vero notum esse non potuisse ex scriptis Mosaicis, imo neque ex propheticis. Respondeo reale Christi sacrificium, id est, illius mortem & vim quam ad illam sacrificia typica habuerunt, mysterium esse quod solum Evangelium revelavit, quodque praecedentibus saeculis tacitum erat, ut pluribus in locis loquitur Apostolus. Ista quidem Apostoli nostri, postquam accessit lux Evangelii, & rerum ipsarum eventus, vaticiniorum optimus interpres, ex Scriptura sacra deduxerunt. At vero antea in umbris legalibus & prophetiarum obscuritate latebant: nec a vulgo fidelium saltem poterant pervideri. Et certe quod jam post ipsius Christi in terris adventum, nihil dum de illius oblatione & morte apud Judaeos innotuerat, tantum abest ut ab initio quicquam de ea re sciverint, inde manifestum est, quod nihil aeque eorum animos a Christo alienaverit, ac cruenta illa oblatio quae in cruce peracta est. Neque id verum est tantum de Judaeis incredulis, sed de piis & fidelibus quoque: Nam Apostoli ipsi paulo ante Christi passionem illum pro nobis moriturum esse nondum intelligebant. Unde est quod, quum de sua morte illis aperte primum loqui coepit, istud a Petro fuerit rejectum magna cum aversatione: Quapropter etiam illum increpuit Christus dicens, Vade a me Satana, ut videre est Matth. 16. Neque tamen quicquam ad salutem necessarium priscis fidelibus defuit: Nam divina revelatio est mensura fidei nostrae, neque Deus a nobis pleniorem fidem exigit, quam possit ex hactenus facta revelatione haberi. Quamdiu ergo mysterium oblationis a Christo peragendae confuse tantum obscure & indistincte revelatum fuit, suffecit ut fideles obscuram tantum & confusam illius fidem haberent. Clara vero & distincta illius mysterii fides post Evangelii promulgationem necessaria demum fuit.
pass_a_gloss: Besides they contend that through the whole course of the Old Testament it was necessary to be known in the Church that the legal sacrifices shadowed forth Christ's future sacrifice. But that could not have been known from the Mosaic writings, nor even from the prophetic. I answer that Christ's real sacrifice, that is, His death and the force which the typical sacrifices had toward it, is a mystery which the Gospel alone revealed, and which was silent in the preceding ages, as the Apostle speaks in many places. Those things indeed our Apostles, after the light of the Gospel came, and the event of the things themselves, the best interpreter of the prophecies, deduced from sacred Scripture. But beforehand they lay hid in the legal shadows and the obscurity of the prophecies: nor could they at least be clearly seen by the common faithful. And certainly that even after Christ's coming on earth nothing yet was known among the Jews of His offering and death — so far are they from having known anything of that matter from the beginning — is plain from this, that nothing equally alienated their minds from Christ as that bloody offering accomplished on the cross. Nor is that true only of unbelieving Jews, but of the pious and faithful also: For the Apostles themselves a little before Christ's passion did not yet understand that He was to die for us. Whence it is that when He first began to speak openly to them of His death, that was rejected by Peter with great aversion: Wherefore also Christ rebuked him saying, Get behind me, Satan, as is seen in Matthew 16. And yet nothing necessary to salvation was lacking to the ancient faithful: For divine revelation is the measure of our faith, nor does God exact from us a fuller faith than can be had from the revelation hitherto made. Therefore as long as the mystery of the offering to be performed by Christ was revealed only confusedly, obscurely and indistinctly, it sufficed that the faithful have only an obscure and confused faith of it. But a clear and distinct faith of that mystery was finally necessary after the promulgation of the Gospel.
pass_b_english: They add: OT believers had to know legal sacrifices foreshadowed Christ's — yet Moses and the prophets do not make that plain.
Answer: Christ's real death and the types' force toward it is a Gospel mystery, silent in prior ages (as Paul says).
Apostles read it from Scripture after Gospel light and fulfillment; before, it lay in shadows — not clear to the common faithful.
Even after Christ came, Jews and even the Apostles did not yet grasp His death — Peter rebuked as Satan (Matthew 16).
Ancient saints lacked nothing needful: revelation measures faith. Obscure confused faith sufficed until the Gospel made clear distinct faith necessary.
